hook_text: There is an antelope in the Kalahari that can go weeks without a drink in forty-degree heat. Here is how.
clip_script: Meet the gemsbok. It lives where rain hardly falls and the sand burns. First, its pale coat bounces the sunlight away. Second, instead of sweating, it lets its body heat up during the day, saving precious water, while blood cooled in its nose protects its brain. Third, it barely wees, and its urine is super concentrated. Fourth, it eats at night, when plants and roots hold more water. That is three kinds of adaptation: body parts, inside body workings and behaviour. Next to it, the quiver tree is a living water bottle with a waxy coat like cling film. And here is the twist. No gemsbok chose any of this. Over thousands of generations, the ones that saved water best survived the droughts and had babies. Every body tells you where it lives.
visual_style: A whiteboard gemsbok under a blazing Sun with four labelled callouts appearing one by one; a quiver tree drawn as a bottle; a family tree of gemsbok fading through generations.
pacing: Four rapid adaptation reveals, a quick plant aside, a thoughtful twist at the end.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and decode the adaptations of any animal you see.
